{{Quote|I am glad I have never visited <u>that</u> tower&mdash;it's a one-way trip to the Agricultural Corps!|[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], in one of his journals|<ref name="Journal">''[[Anakin Skywalker: A Jedi's Journal]]''</ref>}}
The '''Reassignment Council Tower''' was the northeastern tower surrounding [[Temple Spire/Legends|Temple Spire]] atop the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Within the [[Reassignment Council Chamber|topmost chamber]] of the Tower was the meeting place of the [[Council of Reassignment/Legends|Council of Reassignment]], one of the four [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Councils]] of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] during the reign of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].

==History==
The Reassignment Council Tower was added to the Temple post [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]] and served the Order for a brief time before it collapsed during the [[Sacking of Coruscant]] in [[3653 BBY]].<ref name="Timeline 1" /> While reconstruction was postponed for several centuries, the Tower was eventually finished during the expansion of [[1019 BBY]]. Serving the Order throughout its next millennia, the Council worked closely with the [[Jedi Service Corps/Legends|Jedi Service Corps]], reassigning Jedi who did not pass their [[Jedi Trials/Legends|Jedi Trials]] to the working force of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="SWCL" />

Surviving the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Tower was ruined when the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] invaded per [[Operation: Knightfall/Legends|Operation: Knightfall]]. Led by [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] laid waste to the complex blasting the Tower from the inside and out, reducing many of its interior chambers to rubble and destroying the polished facade.<ref name="ROTS" /> Standing abandoned for the next several decades, the Tower eventually crumbled during the disaster involving the ''[[Lusankya/Legends|Lusankya]]'' after the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] conquered Coruscant.<ref name="The New Jedi Order: Dark Tide II: Ruin">''[[The New Jedi Order: Dark Tide II: Ruin]]''</ref> The rest of the Temple would eventually crumble during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], but eventually saw reconstruction under the leadership of the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]]. Using blueprints salvaged from the ruined [[Jedi Archives/Legends|Jedi Archives]], the [[Reconstruction Authority]] [[New Jedi Temple|rebuilt]] the Ziggurat, towers and all, although they were now concealed behind a [[Transparisteel/Legends|transparisteel]]-and-stone exterior.<ref name="FOTJO" />

==Layout==
Located on the northeast corner of the Temple, the Reassignment Council Tower was designed to symbolize unity and the steps to enlightenment each Jedi must take. The masonry of the spire was supported by a highly-tensile substance known as [[Magnite/Legends|magnite]], which aided in the support of the thin frame of the tower. The tower was crowned by a Council Chamber, like to that in each of the other three Council towers of the Temple. Atop the spire were a series of reception/transmission antennas which, along with a constant connection to the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]], tapped into the cosmic energy fields of the galaxy itself in order to stay in contact with Jedi on far-flung planets. The central topmast of this unique array of antennas was a powerful multi-frequency [[Eradicator (communications scrambler)|eradicator]]/scrambler that when coupled with the eradicators incorporated into the tower's frame scrambled all communications in and out of the Temple. Communication bundles in the wall cavities fed data from these masts, through the columns within the Council chambers, to the [[High Council holomap room|Operations Planning Center]]. Receiver vanes within the walls of the spire converted signals from [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] locations into real-space coordinates before displaying them on the map.<ref name="SWCL" />

Ascending from the base of the tower was a dedicated [[Turbolift/Legends|turbolift]] crafted by great Jedi architects to incorporate Force-inspired, internal dynamics, allowing for the different sizes and shapes of the Order's members to ascend the narrow spire.<ref name="SWCL" /> At the base of tower was a [[Jedi Temple/Legends|reception and entrance hall]] leading from the roof of the Temple Ziggurat into the center of the tower. Two large [[Bronzium/Legends|bronzium]] statues flanked the entrance; their lightsabers crossed over the entry, lifting to allow access to the Tower.<ref name="TFU" /> The hall beyond was dotted with six bronzium statues of long dead Jedi, with two doors to either side, leading to curved halls. A large memorial statue was held in the cavernous center shaft of the Tower, held by repulsorpads. A bridge spanned the lofty shaft of the tower, passing around the chest of the statue and into a chamber on the other side. Near the top of the tower, three Contemplation Stations were spaced evenly from each other to provide a meditative retreat for Jedi preparing to go before the Council.<ref name="SWCL" />

Each spire was also equipped with a [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]]; though they would be completely refurbished just before the Clone Wars began. A landing platform extended from the hangar mouth, allowing for ships to land and depart away from the Tower's structure. Located fifteen stories below the council chambers, the hangars were connected with a small garage that serviced the space craft. Also within the Tower were the chambers and offices of Jedi Council members.<ref name="SWCL" />
